## Why

Pull request 154 (native context intents and current relationship packets) reached its round limit. The last CodeRabbit review (head c59277c) raised four more findings. They harden the proof harness and widen parity coverage; none is a defect in the native context feature itself.

## Findings to close

1. **Heavy lift** — `scripts/context-proof-process.mts`: never signal a process ID that may have been reused. Verify process identity (start time or a pidfd where available) before each escalation signal.
2. `scripts/context-review-revert.mts`: keep the oracle configuration when starting proof subprocesses.
3. `tests/orientation_differential.rs`: add a tracker initialized by the current pm to the parity matrix.
4. `tests/support/read_output_unit.rs`: check that metadata is kept at the 5,000-token budget.

## Acceptance

- Each finding has a regression that fails on revert.
- The pid-reuse guard works on Linux, macOS and Windows runners.
- Coverage stays at the 100% floor.


---

### GitHub comments (3)

> **@unbraind** (2026-11-09T13:15:42Z)
>
> More hardening findings from the review of head c59277c, for the same follow-up:
> 
> 5. `scripts/context-revert-helpers.mts:60`: report symlink resolution errors in proof copies instead of skipping them.
> 6. `tests/support/orientation_context_unit.rs:56`: require the intent receipt for retained SDK packets.
> 7. `tests/support/orientation_packet_unit.rs:835`: test reservation boundaries below the full threshold.
> 
> The two behavioral parity findings from that review (focus classifications across compaction probes, and whole-settings validation before the activity fallback) stay in pull request 154, where they are being fixed.

> **@unbraind** (2026-11-09T14:53:38Z)
>
> More harness and test findings from the review of head 4502aa2. These belong to the same follow-up; some re-raise items 4, 6 and 7.
> 
> 8. `scripts/context-proof-process.mts`:
>    - track the child before writing its registry entry (:219);
>    - bound the wait after termination fails (:235);
>    - keep timeout errors after draining (:282, marked IMPORTANT by the reviewer).
> 9. `scripts/context-revert-helpers.mts:32`: check that each mutation run fails on the expected assertion.
> 10. `scripts/context-review-revert.mts:18`: keep the interpreter override in proof subprocesses.
> 11. `scripts/context-review-safety.test.mts:339`: test the Windows argument round trip.
> 12. `tests/orientation_differential.rs:2215`: add an intent parity fixture initialized by the current CLI.
> 13. Re-raised: `tests/support/read_output_unit.rs:840` (5000-token metadata, item 4), `tests/support/orientation_context_unit.rs:56` (intent receipt, item 6), and `tests/support/orientation_packet_unit.rs:835` (reservation threshold, item 7).

> **@unbraind** (2026-11-09T16:11:44Z)
>
> More harness and test findings from the review of head 7b1d9fd:
> 
> 14. `scripts/context-proof-process.mts`:
>     - keep diagnostics when the Windows wrapper fails to start a command (:117);
>     - support draining without `ps` (:133);
>     - keep the timeout and output-limit diagnostics (:251).
> 15. `scripts/context-real.mts`:
>     - capture the snapshot before checking the driver version (:37);
>     - reject signal-terminated intent comparisons (:123).
> 16. `scripts/context-revert-helpers.mts:60`: report symlink resolution errors (re-raises item 5).
> 17. `scripts/context-safety-revert.mts:15`: check the oracle installations before copying the worktree.
> 18. `tests/orientation_differential.rs`:
>     - add an intent comparison with current initialization (:2215, re-raises item 12);
>     - run the alias checks from a different directory (:3039).
> 19. `tests/pagination_differential.rs:153`: assert the terminal receipt without the oracle.
> 20. `tests/support/read_output_unit.rs:839`: run the preservation assertion at the generous budget (re-raises item 4).
> 
> The two native findings from that review (`src/orientation_context/sections.rs:77` settings validation, and `src/cli.rs:144` argument roles) stay in pull request 154.
Harden proof-harness process signalling against PID reuse and widen context parity coverage
